name: SugarClock
subtitle: Your clock, your way
promotional_text: Set up your SugarClock nearby, personalize its display, and review changes before updating. Requires a compatible SugarClock device.
description:
Make your SugarClock feel like yours.

SugarClock is the iOS companion for a Ulanzi TC001 running Bluetooth-capable SugarClock firmware. Hardware is required and sold separately. Use your iPhone or iPad to find a nearby clock, pair using the code on its display, and manage its settings.

KEEP YOUR CLOCKS TOGETHER
Save and name multiple clocks. Return to the one you want without looking up its IP address or joining a temporary Wi-Fi network.

EDIT AT YOUR PACE
After loading a clock once, continue editing its saved settings even while disconnected. Review pending changes, remove individual edits, then tap Update clock. The app confirms when settings have been saved on the clock.

MAKE IT YOURS
Adjust brightness, units, display preferences, time settings and clock alerts. Choose from seven Pixel Pets on compatible firmware. Configure Wi-Fi, Dexcom Share or a custom URL / compatible Nightscout source without replacing credentials you leave unchanged.

LET YOUR CLOCK GET ON WITH ITS DAY
Your clock fetches readings using its own Wi-Fi. Its display and configured alerts continue to run when the app is closed. The app uses foreground Bluetooth sessions and can request signed firmware updates through the clock's supported Wi-Fi update service.

BEFORE YOU START
Requires iOS/iPadOS 17 or later and compatible SugarClock firmware. Older clocks may need a USB or supported OTA upgrade before the app can discover them. Wi-Fi, internet access and a working provider connection are required for new readings. Provider accounts, terms and availability are separate from SugarClock. New Libre-specific settings currently remain in the clock's web interface.

No SugarClock account or subscription is required. Firmware fleet reporting and data-provider connections are described in the privacy policy.

SugarClock configures a companion display. It does not measure glucose, calculate insulin doses, or replace your primary glucose device, its alarms, or professional medical advice. Consult your healthcare professional for medical decisions.
